internal_discovery.plain_explanation: The root-id ا ن ي bundles at least four Quran-internally unbridged word-classes: (1) the grammaticalized interrogative/free-choice particle أَنَّىٰ 'how / by what means / whence' (28 of 36 tokens, a closed-class function word whose content is supplied by its complement, not by any recoverable root seme); (2) a small temporal/attainment field — ءَانَاء 'periods/watches of the night' (20:130, 39:9, 3:113), the noun إِنَىٰ 'its due readiness' (33:53), and the verb يَأْنِ 'the time has come due' (57:16); (3) ءَانٍ/ءَانِيَة 'boiling, at peak heat' (55:44, 88:5); and (4) ءَانِيَة 'silver vessels/containers' (76:15). The only proposed unifier ('a thing reaching its due point, in time or degree') collapses because it cannot absorb the concrete container (76:15) or the grammaticalized particle without importing an etymological abstraction the co-text never supplies — forbidden by the source policy. No single Quran-internal nucleus spans all 36 occurrences; the honest verdict is a multi-class partition with no safe bridge.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: The root-id does NOT denote one concept. أَنَّىٰ (Class A) does not entail time, vessel, or heat and is not 'who/what/when' — it interrogates manner/source and once (2:223) licenses free choice; its 'impossibility' force is contextual, not lexical. The night-watches sense (ءَانَاء) is only ever of ٱلَّيْل and does not extend to manner-interrogation, container, or heat. 'Boiling' (D) is about intensity/temperature, carried in co-text by حَمِيم/حَامِية, and does not entail any temporal sense. 'Vessel' (E) entails neither time, manner, nor heat. Identical vocalized surface آنية does NOT fix meaning (76:15 'vessel' vs 88:5 'boiling'), so morphology/orthography is not a semantic-class proxy here.

The decisive evidence is the near-minimal pair 76:15 (vessel) vs 88:5 (boiling): identical surface آنية, mutually irreducible senses, no bridging context — this refutes 'same surface/same root => one meaning' within the very root.
